mainTopic: How far כבוד הבריות reaches: the case of מת מצוה and why it cannot be used as a general rule, followed by רב פפא's question to אביי about why earlier generations received miracles and his own generation does not.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the ברייתא from 19b. A person on his way to bring his קרבן פסח or circumcise his son may not become impure even for his sister, but he must become impure to bury a מת מצוה. The גמרא asks how human dignity can push aside a מצוה, given ״אין חכמה ואין תבונה ואין עצה לנגד ה׳״. It answers that a פסוק says so directly, and that no general rule can be learned from this, because the case is only שב ואל תעשה. Next רב פפא asks אביי why earlier generations had miracles and his does not, even though his generation learns more Torah. אביי answers that the earlier generations were ready to give their lives for קידוש השם, and the גמרא illustrates this with the story of רב אדא בר אהבה. Stories follow about רב גידל and רבי יוחנן sitting at the טבילה gates. In רבי יוחנן's story the גמרא gives several reasons why the עין הרע has no power over יוסף's descendants. The amud ends with the start of a new משנה: נשים, עבדים, and קטנים are exempt from קריאת שמע. The משנה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא ends: he does become impure for a מת מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא from 19b concludes. A person on his way to slaughter his קרבן פסח or circumcise his son may not become impure even for his sister, but he does become impure to bury a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he does become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a ברייתא quoted on the previous page. It sets up the question the גמרא is about to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא (19b) uses the extra words of the פסוק (written about a נזיר) to teach a case: a person on his way to bring his קרבן פסח or circumcise his son may not become impure even for a close relative such as his sister, because he would lose the מצוה. Reading ״וְלַאֲחוֹתוֹ״ closely, it says that only for her may he not become impure, but for a מת מצוה (a dead body with nobody else to bury it) he must. So in this case the dignity of the dead pushes aside his פסח or מילה.

keyTerms.meaning: An unattended dead body with no one else to bury it; everyone must bury it

phrases.english: But he does become impure for a מת מצוה.
phrases.notes: The end of the ברייתא learned from ״וְלַאֲחוֹתוֹ״ (Bamidbar 6:7).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun at the end of 19b, which was brought into the discussion of כבוד הבריות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One on his way to bring his פסח or circumcise his son, who may not become impure for his relatives, must become impure to bury a מת מצוה.

steps.title: Why not apply 'There is no wisdom against God'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. Human dignity should not override a Torah command, because ״אין חכמה ואין תבונה ואין עצה לנגד ה׳״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? Let us say: 'There is no wisdom, no understanding, and no counsel against God!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ruling it just quoted. It asks how burying a dead person, which is about human dignity, can push aside a Torah prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא used this verse to teach that human considerations never override God's commands. Burying a מת מצוה is a matter of כבוד הבריות. So the ruling that it overrides the Torah מצוה of פסח or מילה seems to contradict that principle.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no wisdom and no understanding (Mishlei 21:30)

phrases.english: Why? Let us say:
'There is no wisdom and no understanding
and no counsel against God!'
phrases.notes: Wherever there is a חילול ה׳, honor of people is pushed aside.

steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that one on his way to bring his פסח or circumcise his son becomes impure for a מת מצוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The principle ״אין חכמה...לנגד ה׳״ says human dignity never overrides a Torah prohibition, yet here it seems to.

steps.title: It is different there: a פסוק says so
steps.stepSummary: The מת מצוה case is different, because the Torah itself teaches it through the word ״וְלַאֲחוֹתוֹ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because it is written 'and for his sister.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The rule does not come from human reasoning; the פסוק itself teaches it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״אין חכמה...לנגד ה׳״ only blocks human logic from overriding God's word. Here, God's own word (״וְלַאֲחוֹתוֹ״, 'only for his sister he may not') makes the exception. So nothing is going 'against God'.

phrases.english: It is different there, for it is written: 'And for his sister.'
phrases.notes: Only for his sister may he not become impure, but he does for a מת מצוה.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Source-based distinction: the exception is written in the פסוק itself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Human dignity was overriding a Torah prohibition by its own force.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah itself creates the exception, so no human reasoning goes against God.

steps.title: Should we learn a general rule from this case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: since the Torah lets dignity override טומאה here, let us learn from it that כבוד הבריות overrides every prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let us learn from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests building a general rule from the מת מצוה case. It is setting up the next step, which will reject the idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah shows that human dignity overrides one prohibition, maybe we can stretch that to all prohibitions. That would undo the principle ״אין חכמה...לנגד ה׳״ everywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us learn from it (and build a general rule)

phrases.english: Then let us learn from it!
phrases.notes: Learn that human dignity overrides all Torah prohibitions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer of step 3 and tries to turn it into a general rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can the מת מצוה exception serve as a source that כבוד הבריות overrides all prohibitions?

steps.title: Holding back from a מצוה is different
steps.stepSummary: No general rule can be learned, because the מת מצוה case is only שב ואל תעשה, a passive failure to keep a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Sit and do not act' is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the attempt to build a general rule. The מת מצוה case belongs to a special, milder category.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By becoming impure for the מת מצוה, the person does not actively break anything. He simply becomes unable to bring his פסח or do the מילה, which is a passive loss and not an active sin. You cannot use that to prove that human dignity may override an active Torah prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Sit and do not act': passively not doing a מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a מת מצוה is unimportant, or that the מצוה of פסח or מילה does not apply. It is saying this case falls into the passive category, so it cannot prove a rule for active violations.
steps.whatToRemember: כבוד הבריות can push aside a Torah law only in a passive (שב ואל תעשה) way, or where a פסוק says so. It does not justify actively breaking a Torah prohibition.

phrases.english: 'Sit and do not act' is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference proposed in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects extending the מת מצוה exception into a general rule for all prohibitions.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source case is passive (שב ואל תעשה), so it cannot teach a rule about actively breaking prohibitions.

steps.title: רב פפא asks: why did the earlier generations get miracles?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי why miracles happened for the earlier generations but do not happen for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: What is different about the earlier generations, for whom miracles happened, and what is different about us, for whom miracles do not happen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shifts to a new question. רב פפא asks why the earlier sages received miracles and his generation does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new branch. It will turn out to connect to self-sacrifice for God's honor, the same theme as the previous discussion. רב פפא now begins to rule out possible explanations.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
What is different about the earlier generations
that miracles happened for them,
and what is different about us
that miracles do not happen for us?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: מַאי שְׁנָא רִאשׁוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion. It is linked in theme to giving up one's own honor for God's honor.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What gave the earlier generations the merit to receive miracles?

steps.title: It cannot be because of Torah learning
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules out Torah study as the reason. In רב יהודה's time they learned mainly סדר נזיקין, and even עוקצין was hard for him, while now they learn all six סדרים and many versions of עוקצין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is because of learning: in the years of רב יהודה, all their learning was in נזיקין, and we learn all six orders. When רב יהודה reached in עוקצין the law 'a woman who pickles a vegetable in a pot', and some say 'olives pickled with their leaves are pure', he would say: 'I see the deep debates of רב and שמואל here.' And we learn עוקצין in thirteen versions.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא knocks down the obvious answer, that the earlier generations learned more Torah. He shows his own generation actually learns more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's generation mostly learned נזיקין, while רב פפא's generation covers all six סדרים. רב יהודה even found a simple-looking law in עוקצין as hard as the great debates of רב and שמואל, while they learn עוקצין thirteen different ways. So greater learning cannot explain the miracles.

keyTerms.meaning: The סדר of damages and civil law
The tractate dealing with stems and impurity of produce
The deep debates of רב and שמואל
Thirteen versions (or study halls) of learning

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not boasting. He is clearing away a wrong answer so that the real question stands out sharply.

phrases.english: If it is because of learning,
in the years of Rav Yehuda
all of their learning was in Nezikin,
while we learn all six orders.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי הֲוָה מָטֵי רַב יְהוּדָה בְּעוּקְצִין,
phrases.english: And when Rav Yehuda would reach, in Okatzin,
'a woman who pickles a vegetable in a pot,'
and some say it was:
'olives pickled with their leaves are pure,'
he would say: 'The deep debates of Rav and Shmuel'
I see here.'
phrases.notes: He found these laws extremely difficult.

phrases.english: And we learn
Okatzin in thirteen versions,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules out one possible answer to the question of step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects Torah learning as the reason for the earlier generations' miracles.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The later generation learns more widely and more deeply, yet does not get miracles.

steps.title: רב יהודה brought rain by removing a shoe; we cry and are not answered
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא sharpens the contrast. When רב יהודה began a fast by taking off one shoe, rain came at once, while his own generation suffers and cries out with no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yet when רב יהודה would take off one of his shoes, rain would come. And we torment ourselves and cry out, and no one notices us.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes his question with a vivid example of how different the two generations are. The next step gives אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking off a shoe was the first step of a public fast for rain. For רב יהודה, that small act alone brought rain. For רב פפא's generation, full fasting and prayer bring nothing, which proves something other than learning made the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Took off one of his shoes (the start of a fast)
And no one pays attention to us

steps.whyThisMatters: The sharp contrast prepares the way for אביי's answer: the earlier generations gave up their own honor for the sake of Heaven. This ties back to the theme of כבוד הבריות versus כבוד שמים.

phrases.english: Whereas Rav Yehuda,
when he would remove one of his shoes,
rain would come,
and we torment ourselves
and cry out loudly,
and no one notices us.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ רַב יְהוּדָה כִּי הֲוָה שָׁלֵיף חַד מְסָאנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the question of step 6 after step 7 ruled out learning as the cause.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the earlier generations were favored with miracles despite learning less
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב יהודה, whose rain came as soon as he removed a shoe

steps.title: אביי's answer: earlier generations gave their lives for God's honor
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the earlier generations were ready to give up their lives for קידוש השם, and his own generation is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב פפא: The earlier generations were ready to give their lives to sanctify God's Name. We are not ready to give our lives to sanctify God's Name.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now answers רב פפא's question from the earlier steps. Miracles depend on self-sacrifice for God's honor, not on the amount of Torah a generation learns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא had already shown that Torah knowledge cannot explain the difference, because his generation learned more. אביי points to a different quality: complete devotion to קידוש השם. That devotion is what earned the earlier generations their miracles.

keyTerms.meaning: The earlier ones, meaning the previous generations
They gave over their lives, meaning they were ready for total self-sacrifice

steps.whatToRemember: Miracles followed the earlier generations' self-sacrifice for God's honor. Their Torah knowledge was not the reason.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the question from steps 6 through 8. It teaches that devotion and sacrifice can count for more than quantity of learning.

phrases.english: He (Abaye) said to him (Rav Pappa):
The earlier generations would give over their lives
for the sanctification of God's Name,
we do not give over our lives
for the sanctification of God's Name.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: קַמָּאֵי הֲווֹ קָא מָסְרִי נַפְשַׁיְיהוּ אַקְּדוּשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question opened in step 6 and sharpened in steps 7 and 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why miracles happened for earlier generations and not for later ones.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The earlier generations were ready to give their lives for קידוש השם, and later ones are not.

steps.title: The story of רב אדא בר אהבה and the forbidden garment
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה tore a garment of כלאים off a woman in the market, thinking she was Jewish. She turned out to be a non-Jew, and he had to pay four hundred זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the story of רב אדא בר אהבה. He saw a woman wearing a garment of כלאים in the market. He thought she was Jewish, so he got up and tore it off her. It turned out she was not Jewish. The court set the payment for her embarrassment at four hundred זוז. He asked her, 'What is your name?' She said, 'מתון.' He said, 'מתון plus מתון (two hundred and two hundred) is worth four hundred זוז.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a real-life example of the earlier generations' self-sacrifice for God's honor. רב אדא acted at once against a public sin, without worrying about the cost to himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא did not stop to protect himself. He acted publicly against what he believed was a Jewish woman wearing כלאים, and he paid heavily for it. His closing remark is a wordplay: in Aramaic, מתון means 'two hundred,' so her name 'doubled' adds up to the four hundred זוז he paid.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish woman, literally a Samaritan woman
A garment of כלאים, a forbidden mix of wool and linen
They assessed it, meaning the court set the amount of the payment

steps.confusionAlert: The final line is a play on words, not a legal ruling. 'מתון' is both her name and the Aramaic word for two hundred.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
phrases.english: Like this story of Rav Adda bar Ahava:
he saw a certain non-Jewish woman
who was wearing a garment of forbidden mixture in the marketplace.
He thought that she was Jewish,
so he stood up and tore it off her.
It became known that she was a non-Jew.
They assessed her damages at four hundred zuz.
He said to her: What is your name?
She said to him: Matun.
He said to her: Matun plus matun (two hundred),
phrases.notes: Wordplay: מתון means 'two hundred' in Aramaic.

phrases.english: is worth four hundred zuz.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates אביי's claim with a concrete story.
steps.raayaObject: The earlier generations were ready to sacrifice themselves for קידוש השם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב אדא בר אהבה tearing off the כלאים garment at personal cost.

steps.title: רב גידל sits at the immersion gates to teach
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל used to sit at the gates of the טבילה sites and tell the women how to immerse properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל would regularly go and sit at the gates of the immersion places. He told the women: Immerse like this, and immerse like that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about a great earlier sage. This step sets up the question the רבנן will ask him next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב גידל placed himself in an awkward spot so that women would perform טבילה correctly. This shows how far the earlier sages would go for the sake of a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: The gates of the immersion sites (מקוה)
Accustomed, meaning he did this regularly

phrases.english: Rav Giddel was accustomed
to go and sit
at the gates of the immersion sites.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הָכִי טְבִילוּ וְהָכִי טְבִילוּ.
phrases.english: He said to them: Immerse this way, and immerse that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב גִּידֵּל הֲוָה רְגִיל דַּהֲוָה קָא אָזֵיל וְיָתֵיב אַשַּׁעֲרֵי דִטְבִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about the greatness and purity of the earlier sages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב גידל would sit at the טבילה gates to teach women how to immerse correctly.

steps.title: The רבנן ask רב גידל about the יצר הרע
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן ask רב גידל whether he is afraid of the יצר הרע in such a place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said to him: Isn't the master afraid of the evil inclination?
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן question whether it is wise for רב גידל to sit in a place that could lead to improper thoughts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is spiritual danger. Sitting near women who are immersing could stir the יצר הרע.

keyTerms.meaning: Master, a respectful way to address a sage

phrases.english: The Sages said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָא קָא מִסְתְּפֵי מָר מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע?
phrases.english: Is the master not afraid of the evil inclination?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לָא קָא מִסְתְּפֵי מָר מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רב גידל's behavior from step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב גידל does not fear the יצר הרע.

steps.title: רב גידל: they look to me like white geese
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל answers that in his eyes the women are like white geese, so he has no improper thoughts.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: In my eyes they look like white geese.
steps.whatsHappening: רב גידל explains that he has no fear, because he feels no attraction at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His spiritual level was so high that the sight did not affect him. That is why he could safely do this for the sake of the מצוה.

phrases.english: He said to them:
In my eyes they are like white geese.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: דָּמְיָין בְּאַפַּאי כִּי קָאקֵי חִיוָּרֵי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The women do not arouse him at all. They are like white geese in his eyes.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן sits at the immersion gates for a blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן sat at the טבילה gates so that women would see him and have children as beautiful as he was.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן would regularly go and sit at the gates of the immersion places. He said: When the daughters of Israel come up from immersion, they will look at me, and they will have children as beautiful as I am.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a similar story about רבי יוחנן. His reason was different from רב גידל's, and this step sets up the רבנן's question to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן was famous for his beauty. He believed that what a woman sees right after טבילה can influence the children she will have. His goal was to bring blessing to Jewish families.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan was accustomed
to go and sit
at the gates of the immersion sites.
He said: When the daughters of Israel come up
and come from immersion,
they will look at me,
and they will have children as beautiful as me.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֲוָה רְגִיל דַּהֲוָה קָא אָזֵיל וְיָתֵיב אַשַּׁעֲרֵי דִטְבִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to רב גידל's, using the same opening wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן sat at the טבילה gates so that women would have beautiful children.

steps.title: The רבנן ask רבי יוחנן about the עין הרע
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן ask רבי יוחנן whether he fears the עין הרע by showing off his beauty.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said to him: Isn't the master afraid of the evil eye?
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן raise a different worry this time. Displaying his beauty in public could bring an עין הרע upon him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב גידל the worry was the יצר הרע. For רבי יוחנן the worry is that others' jealous or admiring eyes could harm him.

keyTerms.meaning: The evil eye (עין הרע), harm caused by jealous or admiring looks

phrases.english: The Sages said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָא קָא מִסְתְּפֵי מָר מֵעֵינָא בִּישָׁא?
phrases.english: Is the master not afraid of the evil eye?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן: לָא קָא מִסְתְּפֵי מָר מֵעֵינָא בִּישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רבי יוחנן's practice from step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוחנן does not fear the עין הרע.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: יוסף's descendants are above the עין הרע
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that he descends from יוסף, over whom the עין הרע has no power. He cites a פסוק, and the גמרא adds רבי אבהו's reading of it to show how the פסוק proves this.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I come from the descendants of יוסף, and the evil eye has no power over them. As it says: 'יוסף is a fruitful vine, a fruitful vine by a spring (עלי עין).' And רבי אבהו said: Do not read it 'עלי עין' (by a spring). Read it 'עולי עין' (rising above the eye).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains why he is safe. As a descendant of יוסף he is protected from the עין הרע, and he backs this up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'עין' can mean either 'spring' or 'eye.' רבי אבהו uses an אל תקרי reading: 'עולי עין' means יוסף's descendants rise above the eye, so the evil eye cannot reach them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do not read' — a method of reading a פסוק with different vowels to draw out a lesson

steps.confusionAlert: אל תקרי does not change the written text of the Torah. It adds a second layer of meaning on top of the plain reading.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אֲנָא מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף קָא אָתֵינָא,
phrases.english: He said to them: I come from the seed of Joseph,
over whom the evil eye has no power,
as it is written: 'Joseph is a fruitful vine,
a fruitful vine by a spring (alei ayin)',
and Rabbi Abbahu said:
Do not read 'alei ayin' (by a spring),
rather 'olei ayin' (rising above the eye).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אֲנָא מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף קָא אָתֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's question about the עין הרע.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יוסף's descendants are not affected by the עין הרע, as shown by the reading 'עולי עין.'

steps.title: A second source: יוסף's descendants are like fish
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא brings a different פסוק, 'וידגו לרב,' to prove that יוסף's descendants are protected from the עין הרע, just as fish hidden under water are.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said the proof comes from here: 'And may they multiply (וידגו) abundantly in the midst of the earth.' Just as the fish in the sea are covered by water and the evil eye has no power over them, so too the evil eye has no power over the descendants of יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second source for the same idea, that the עין הרע cannot harm יוסף's descendants. Here the proof is from the blessing יעקב gave to יוסף's sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וידגו' sounds like 'דגים,' meaning fish. Fish are hidden under water, so no eye can see them and the evil eye cannot reach them. יוסף's descendants share that protection.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, meaning from this verse
And may they multiply; related to the word דָּג, fish

steps.whatToRemember: Two sources teach that the עין הרע has no power over יוסף's descendants: רבי אבהו's reading 'עולי עין' and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's comparison of them to fish hidden under water.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אֲמַר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said: From here:
'And may they multiply abundantly in the midst of the earth',
just as the fish in the sea —
water covers them
and the evil eye has no power over them,
so too the seed of Joseph —
the evil eye has no power over them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אֲמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק as the source for the same idea.
steps.raayaObject: The עין הרע has no power over יוסף's descendants.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'וידגו לרב בקרב הארץ,' comparing יוסף's descendants to fish hidden under water.

steps.title: Another reason: יוסף's eye did not desire what was not his
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another explanation for why the עין הרע has no power over יוסף. His eye refused to enjoy what did not belong to him, meaning he refused אשת פוטיפר. So no evil eye can rule over him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: an eye that did not want to feast on what was not its own, the evil eye has no power over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different reason why יוסף and his descendants are safe from the עין הרע. This reason is based on how יוסף behaved, not on a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 16-17 proved the protection from פסוקים. This step explains why יוסף earned it. He held back his eyes from אשת פוטיפר, who was not his, so measure for measure, other people's evil eyes cannot harm him or his children.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces another possible explanation

steps.whatToRemember: יוסף is protected from עין הרע for two reasons. The פסוקים say so, and he guarded his own eyes from what was not his, so others' eyes cannot harm him.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
An eye that did not want to feast
on that which is not its own
the evil eye has no power over it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a reason-based alternative to the פסוק-based proofs in Steps 16-17
steps.raayaObject: That the עין הרע cannot rule over יוסף and his descendants
steps.raayaSupportSource: יוסף's restraint with אשת פוטיפר, a measure-for-measure reasoning

steps.title: New משנה: women, slaves, and minors are exempt from קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. It rules that נשים, עבדים, and קטנים do not have to say קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Women, slaves, and minors are exempt from reciting קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The אגדה has ended, and a new משנה starts with a new topic. It tells us who is not obligated in קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three groups are listed together: נשים, עבדים, and קטנים. They often share similar exemptions in מצוות. The גמרא will later explain why each is exempt from קריאת שמע. This passage shows only the opening of the משנה, which continues with more rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: marks the start of a משנה
Slaves: here, a non-Jewish slave owned by a Jew, who keeps some מצוות
Minors: children under the age of מצוות

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה continues on the next amud with more rulings, for example about תפילין, תפילה, and מזוזה. Do not treat this line as the whole משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the basic source for the halachic rule that נשים, עבדים, and קטנים are exempt from קריאת שמע.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Women, slaves, and minors
are exempt from the recitation of Shema

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים וּקְטַנִּים פְּטוּרִין מִקְּרִיאַת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the aggadic section and opens a new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נשים, עבדים, and קטנים are exempt from קריאת שמע
